mentions.excerpt: Depressed valuations for Oracle and CoreWeave were already pricing that discomfort.
Meta was 22 percent below, Oracle 54 percent below.

Quanta 72 compares Cisco, EMC, Oracle and Sun with Nvidia, Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon and points to the difference: the dot-com suppliers depended on customers who could stop buying, while today’s spenders fund the buildout from advertising, cloud, software and e-commerce.
That is the market’s split in one glance: Nvidia and Micron have been paid for scarcity; Alphabet, Meta and Oracle have been charged for financing.
Oracle’s backlog is about half OpenAI.
In Ren’s account, Bloom got Oracle running in 55 days.
On September 24, Oracle sent a letter to a unit of Blue Owl Capital about Project Jupiter, a 2.45-gigawatt New Mexico campus being built for the Stargate venture with OpenAI.
The notice invokes force majeure and would let Oracle defer payments if the site misses its 2028 opening.
Oracle says the project is on schedule; Blue Owl says the notice changes none of the financial commitments.

Kakashii, on September 24, reads Oracle's first fiscal quarter the other way: most of the $26 billion rise in remaining performance obligations came prepaid or with the customer's own hardware, so the new contracts need no incremental capital from Oracle.

And Kakashii's September 24 point about Oracle is the strongest word on this side: most of the new obligations arrived prepaid or with the customer's own hardware, so they depend on no one raising capital.

Tower's $290 million is in hand and most of Oracle's $26 billion came prepaid, while Ciena's secured supply is a commitment to its suppliers that depends on its customers keeping theirs through fiscal 2029.
